final_candidates.decision_summary: A222V corresponds to the well-known 677C>T MTHFR variant that causes marked thermolability and strongly reduced enzyme activity. It is the strongest single-substitution loss-of-function candidate while preserving protein expression.
E429A corresponds to the 1298A>C variant associated with reduced MTHFR activity. It impairs function without abolishing protein viability.

R594 lies in the S-adenosylmethionine regulatory domain; replacing the charged arginine with glutamine likely disrupts regulatory-domain interactions and reduces activity. Confidence is moderate given the lack of external evidence.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates are established natural/validated loss-of-function MTHFR substitutions and further self-iteration without evidence would not improve the ranking.

history.rationale: Well-characterized common variant that destabilizes the catalytic domain and substantially reduces MTHFR activity; likely tolerable to folding yet strongly impairs function.
A222V is a well-known natural MTHFR variant (677C>T, Ala to Val) that markedly reduces enzyme activity and thermolability, directly matching the loss-of-function goal.
Established polymorphism (Ala variant) associated with significantly decreased enzyme activity in the regulatory domain.
E429A (1298A>C variant) is a documented reduced-activity MTHFR variant; it impairs activity while leaving the protein expressed and viable.
Known deleterious variant impairing FAD binding and catalytic efficiency; strong candidate for loss of function.
R594 is near the S-adenosylmethionine regulatory domain; substituting a glutamine removes an arginine side chain and likely destabilizes/regulatory-domain function, reducing activity.
Isoleucine adjacent to the FAD isoalloxazine ring in the catalytic domain; bulky substitution can disrupt FAD positioning and hydride transfer.
I153 sits near the folate-binding region but Ile-to-Met is a conservative substitution with uncertain impact on activity; confidence is downgraded.
